text:
Toronto and Vancouver arrive on opposite slides. The Maple Leafs lost 5-4 at SEA on Wednesday when Brandon Montour scored with 0:33 left, and they're 3-2-0 in their last five while missing Kirill Marchenko and John Tavares. The Canucks are 1-4-0 over the same stretch after the Sharks came back from two goals down to beat them 3-2. Teddy Blueger, who played 185 games for Vancouver, returns tonight as a visitor.

Neither team has been creating enough. At five on five, TOR has taken 45% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and VAN 40%, and Vancouver gives up 3.90 per 60 minutes. Toronto's power play looks stronger (0.71 expected goals a game to 0.53), though the Leafs take 4.6 penalties a game, which hands the Canucks chances. Our model has TOR at 3.44 expected goals tonight and VAN at 2.89. In net, projected starters Anthony Stolarz (+1.57 goals saved above expected, meaning saves beyond what the shot quality predicts) and Leevi Meriläinen (+0.65) both hold small positives this season, after negative years in 2025-26.

Auston Matthews (42% to score) and William Nylander (41%) lead Toronto. Nylander is up to 22:13 a night with Marchenko out, and Easton Cowan has stepped in beside him. For Vancouver, Elias Pettersson is on a six-game point streak and Filip Hronek is two points from 300 career. Our under-the-radar pick is Linus Karlsson, a third-liner with 2.9 expected goals in his last 10 games and seven high-danger shots, 20% to score.
